Label Studio is an annotating software that runs on your computer that will
allow you to annotate images.

## Installation

### Install Environment Manager

I use conda, which can be downloaded by following the links below. The next steps will assume you are using conda.

- [macOS](https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/stable/user-guide/install/macos.html)
- [Windows](https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/stable/user-guide/install/windows.html)

But any environment manager will work. 

### Create an Environment

In your terminal, run the following command:
(The terminal app on Mac or Windows)

```bash
conda create -n label_studio python=3.11
```
You only need to do this once.

> **Note:** Python 3.11 is confirmed to work with Label Studio. 

### Activate Environment 

Run the following to activate the environment. You'll see the environment name in () on the left in the terminal.

```bash
conda activate label_studio
```

### Install Label Studio

Make sure you have installed pip, so that you can install Label Studio.

```bash
conda install pip
```

Now run: 

```bash
pip install label-studio
```

### Start the app

See below for how to run the program.

> **Note:** To read the images straight from the Box folder, start the app with the commands in
> [Using the Box Folder](#using-the-box-folder) instead.

## Using the Box Folder

Label Studio can read the images straight from the Box folder on your computer.

### Box setup

Skip this if the Box folder already shows up on your computer.

1. Download **Box Drive** from [box.com/resources/downloads](https://www.box.com/resources/downloads)
   (Pick the Mac or Windows version) and run the installer.
2. Open Box Drive and sign in with your Box account.
3. Find the Box folder:
   - **Mac:** in the Finder sidebar, under **Locations** → **Box**.
   - **Windows:** in File Explorer, under **Box** in the left pane (it is the folder `C:\Users\<you>\Box`).
4. Open it and find the folder with the images. If it isn't there, ask Connor to share it with your Box account.

### Images on your computer
If Label Studio isn't loading your images or is running slowly, do the following. 

Right-click the folder with the images (in Finder or File Explorer) and choose **Always keep on device**.
Box Drive starts downloading the folder to your computer. 
Without this, Box only downloads each image the first time it is opened, which makes Label Studio slow and can leave images blank until the download finishes.

> **Note:** This keeps a full copy of the folder on your computer, so make sure there is enough disk space.
> To free it up later, right-click the folder and choose **Free up space**.

### Start Label Studio with access to Box

Use these commands instead of plain `label-studio`, every time you start the app:

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### Mac

In Terminal:

```bash
conda activate label_studio
export LABEL_STUDIO_LOCAL_FILES_SERVING_ENABLED=true
export LABEL_STUDIO_LOCAL_FILES_DOCUMENT_ROOT="$HOME/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box"
label-studio
```

> **Mac:** `Box-Box` is where Box Drive keeps your Box files (on older macOS versions it is `~/Box`). 
The first time, macOS may ask whether Terminal can access Box files. Click **Allow**.

#### Windows

In the **terminal**, replace `<you>` with your Windows username:

```bat
conda activate label_studio
set LABEL_STUDIO_LOCAL_FILES_SERVING_ENABLED=true
set LABEL_STUDIO_LOCAL_FILES_DOCUMENT_ROOT=C:\\Users\\<you>\\Box
label-studio
```
> **Windows:** Type the backslashes doubled (`\\`), as Label Studio's documentation does, and don't put quotes around the path. 
> If your Box folder is somewhere other than `C:\Users\<you>\Box`, use that path instead.

:::

> **Note:** Press <kbd>Control</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd> in the terminal to quit the application.

> **Note:** While it is running, Label Studio can read anything under the document root, so don't point it at a bigger folder than you need.



## Beginning a New Project

1. **Create New Project**
2. **Add a project name**
   - Name it after the image folder name.
3. **Data Import**
   - Since we will be pulling the images straight from Box, you can skip this tab (see [how to connect to the Box folder](#connect_to_box)).
   - If you are not using Box, drag and drop all the images into it.
4. **Labeling setup**
   - Select **"Object Detection with Bounding Boxes"**.
   - Switch the editor on the right from **Visual** to **Code**, delete everything in it, and paste in the following, depending on what you are annotating:

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### Objects

   ```xml
   <View>
     <Image name="image" value="$image"/>
     <RectangleLabels name="label" toName="image">
       <Label value="Car" category="0"/>
       <Label value="Bike" category="1"/>
       <Label value="Door" category="2"/>
       <Label value="Garage" category="3"/>
       <Label value="Aux Vehicle" category="4"/>
     </RectangleLabels>
   </View>
   ```

   | Number | Label       |
   |:------:|:------------|
   | 0      | Car         |
   | 1      | Bike        |
   | 2      | Door        |
   | 3      | Garage      |
   | 4      | Aux Vehicle |
   > *Aux Vehicles* include, but are not limited to, the following: Scooter (electric), Boat, Trailer, ATV, RV.

#### Building Classification
   ```xml
   <View>
     <Image name="image" value="$image"/>
     <RectangleLabels name="label" toName="image">
       <Label value="Residential" category="0"/>
       <Label value="Commercial" category="1"/>
       <Label value="Apartment" category="2"/>
       <Label value="Church" category="3"/>
       <Label value="Aux Building" category="4"/>
     </RectangleLabels>
   </View>
   ```

   | Number | Label       |
   |:------:|:------------|
   | 0      | Residential |
   | 1      | Commercial  |
   | 2      | Apartment   |re
   | 3      | Church      |
   | 4      | Aux Building |
   > *Aux Buildings* include, but are not limited to, the following: sheds. 
:::
   > **Important:** Use the same order and number for labels every time.
   > Each annotation will be defined by a number.
   > Label Studio only saves the label's name, and works out the number when you export. 
   > Without a `category`, it numbers the labels alphabetically, so adding a label later would renumber the others.
   > Not keeping numbers and labels lined up across annotations will ruin the object detection model training.

   To add a label later, add it as the **last** `<Label>` line with the next number (e.g. `<Label value="Shed" category="5"/>`). 
   Never change or reuse an existing number, and keep the lines in number order.

5. **Save Project.** This will take you to the annotation list.

### Connect the folder to a project {#connect_to_box}

Do this after step 5 of [Beginning a New Project](#beginning-a-new-project), once the project is saved with its labeling code in place.

1. Open the project, then go to **Settings** → **Cloud Storage** → **Add Source Storage**.
2. Choose **Local Files** and click **Next**.
3. **Storage Title:** the name of the image folder.
4. **Absolute local path:** it starts out filled in with the document root. Add the rest of the path to the
   image folder, for example:
   - **Mac:** `/Users/<you>/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/<folder with the images>`
   - **Windows:** `C:\\Users\\<you>\\Box\\<folder with the images>`

   Click **Test connection**.
5. **Import Method:** choose **Files**, which makes one task per image.
6. **File Name Filter:** `.*\.(jpg|JPG|jpeg|JPEG|png)`
7. Turn on **Scan all sub-folders** if the images are spread over several folders.
8. Click **Load preview** to check the images being read, then **Save & Sync**.

One task per image should now show up in the **Data Manager**. 
To add more images later, put them in the Box folder and sync the storage again from **Settings** → **Cloud Storage**.

> **Note:** Don't rename, move, or delete the images in Box after importing them, because each task points at the image's path.
>
> If images show up blank, check that Box has finished downloading the folder, that the path is inside the document root, and that Label Studio was started with the commands above.

## Annotating Images

### Standards

- Make sure the entire object is in the bounding box. 
  There will be things that are not the object in each bounding box, but try to limit it.

- Annotate every instance of each object in the photo, even if it's related to another house — such as a car in the neighboring house's driveway, or a door on a neighboring house.
  When training the software, it doesn't matter if everything relates to the subject.
  - This also applies to objects that are only partly in a picture. 
    The object detection model will still detect these.

- Again, labels must always have the same numbers associated with them, such as 0 for Car.

### Exporting

1. In project view, press **Export** in the top right corner.
2. Scroll down and press **Yolo with Images**, then press export. 
3. Rename the downloaded ZIP file to match the photo folder, with the prefix changed to "annotated".
4. Upload the ZIP file to the `Annotated Photos` Box folder.
